topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease, exploring the conceptual balance between intrinsic bad luck, inherited genetics, and environmental exposures supported by global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Biological and Molecular Mechanisms of Carcinogens, Initiators, and Promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific infectious, physical, and chemical carcinogens alongside the molecular mechanisms of DNA damage, xenobiotic metabolism, tumor promotion, and host tissue susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the experimental and epidemiological methods used to determine carcinogenicity, including mutational signature sequencing, biobanks, animal toxicology studies, and in vitro Ames testing.

topics.label: Course Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic summarizes the main themes of the lecture and frames environmental cancer risk within everyday decision-making.
